tier_reason: First-party README chart (result_h800-1704017465770.png) against cuSPARSE 12.2 (CSR ALG2/ALG3/default, COO) and GE-SpMM on an H800. The harness is public (test/test_all.cpp run by run.sh: 20 warm-up and 200 timed runs with CUDA events) and the flags are in CMakeLists.txt and cmake/public/CUDA.cmake, but the toolchain actually used is given only as 'NVCC >= 11.8', no host CPU is named, and the reorder files come from an unpublished step. The IPDPS 2023 paper could make it B, but it covers the earlier version and could not be opened (cse.ust.hk blocked by egress). So C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README bar chart (GFLOPS averaged over K = 32, 64, 128 on an H800; values read off the chart, so approximate): HP-SpMM is the highest bar on all 17 datasets, e.g. about 1730 vs about 1050 for the best cuSPARSE variant on Yelp, about 1870 vs 1130 on arxiv, about 3000 vs 1920 on reddit; about equal on ddi (about 2400 vs 2370) and only slightly above GE-SpMM on protein (about 2950 vs 2850; best cuSPARSE about 2150). No exact numbers are printed.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: NVCC >= 11.8 (stated as a minimum; the toolkit actually used is not given beyond 'cuSPARSE-12.2') via CMake. CMakeLists.txt builds Release with host -O3. cmake/public/CUDA.cmake adds -gencode arch=compute_80,code=sm_80, -gencode arch=compute_90,code=sm_90, -std=c++11 and --expt-extended-lambda.
corrections.hardware: NVIDIA H800 for the README figure (host CPU not stated); code requires Ampere (A100, A800) or Hopper (H100, H800) GPUs
corrections.license: Apache-2.0 via per-file headers on the HP-SpMM sources (spmm/mm/spmm_kernel.cu, spmm/mm/spmm_common.cpp, include/spmm/mm/*, test/*.cpp). The repo has no LICENSE file. The bundled starml framework headers (e.g. include/starml/basic/matrix.h, allocator.h) and include/spmm/utils/timer_cuda.h carry no license. The integrated GE-SpMM baseline code is MIT upstream.
corrections.stars_or_usage: 8 stars, 0 forks (an identical copy at https://github.com/HPMLL/HP-SpMM has 5 stars, 1 fork)
corrections.caveats: Results are only a chart image, and the README calls the code an updated version of the IPDPS 2023 method; the paper (DOI 10.1109/IPDPS54959.2023.00057) was not opened. Not like-for-like input: HP-SpMM (LBSpMM in spmm/mm/spmm_kernel.cu) runs on a COO matrix whose rows are permuted by a precomputed '.cugraph_reorder' file, while cuSPARSE and GE-SpMM get the original order. The reorder cost is excluded, and the reorder files exist only as downloads from a personal SharePoint (dataset/download.sh); no generator script is in the repo. The correctness check (CHECK_RES) is commented out in test/test_all.cpp by default. Values are unweighted (all 1.0). No LICENSE file: the kernel sources carry Apache-2.0 headers but the bundled starml framework does not. cuSPARSE is a vendor library, not one of the listed incumbents. CUDA_ARCHITECTURES is set to 80 on the target while CUDA.cmake also adds sm_90 gencode.

notes: Chart values in the record match the image within reading error, and HP-SpMM does top every dataset. The license is better than the record said: Apache-2.0 headers on the core sources, so it is 'mixed' rather than 'reference'. Main shortcoming to record: the row reordering (precomputed, untimed, supplied only to HP-SpMM) is not given to the cuSPARSE baselines. github.com/HPMLL/HP-SpMM is an identical copy (same README, 6 commits); treat it as the same project.

tier_reason: Upgraded from C. The PDF is the peer-reviewed IPDPS Workshops 2021 (GrAPL) paper: a WebSearch returns IEEE Xplore document 9460674 under the same title, matching the batch-37 cuBool finding. Its Tables II and III compare cuBool and clBool against SuiteSparse:GraphBLAS, CUSP, cuSPARSE and clSPARSE. The benchmark code (EgorOrachyov/SpBench) and the CPU and GPU models are public, but no GCC or CUDA versions or flags are stated, so not A.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Abstract: Boolean-specialized matrix-matrix multiplication 'can be up to 5 times faster and consume up to 4 times less memory' than general-purpose operations from CUSP or cuSPARSE. Table II, M x M time in ms, cuBool vs SuiteSparse: 1.9 vs 7.9 (wing), 2.4 vs 3.1 (luxembourg_osm), 23.2 vs 257.6 (amazon0312), 33.3 vs 369.5 (amazon-2008), 41.8 vs 673.3 (web-Google), 18.1 to 35.3 vs 56.9 to 114.5 on the road graphs. That is about 1.3x to 16x across all 10 matrices (derived from page data). cuSPARSE took 4761.3 ms on web-Google. clBool beats cuBool on luxembourg_osm and all five road graphs, and cuSPARSE beats cuBool on luxembourg_osm (1.7 vs 2.4 ms). Table III, M + M^2: cuBool beats SuiteSparse on 9 of 10 matrices (about 1.5x to 3.7x, derived from page data; 1.7 vs 1.6 ms on luxembourg_osm), but CUSP or cuSPARSE beat cuBool on luxembourg_osm and every road graph (e.g. roadNet-PA 16.9 vs CUSP 11.2 ms). There, cuBool's advantage is lower memory.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Not stated in the paper. SpBench README: GCC and CUDA Toolkit (versions not stated), CMake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
corrections.caveats: Already filed in decisions.json as a duplicate of cuBool (https://github.com/sparselinearalgebra/cubool). SPbLA bundles the cuBool and clBool backends and rests on the same GrAPL 2021 tables, and SpBench benchmarks the standalone cuBool and clBool libraries, not the spbla umbrella build. The paper itself says the comparison is not entirely fair: Boolean kernels against float kernels, and a GTX 1070 GPU against SuiteSparse:GraphBLAS on a 4-core i7-6700. SuiteSparse version and thread count are not stated. Compiler versions and flags are not stated. Each result is an average of 10 runs. Abandoned: last commit 2022-08-19. The README Performance charts (docs/pictures/mxm-perf-time.svg) are path-rendered SVGs and were not read.

notes: Every number the record quotes matches Tables II and III of the PDF, and its 4x-16x ratios are correct for the matrices it chose. The full range is 1.3x to 16x. Tier raised to B on the confirmed IPDPSW 2021 venue, the same evidence as cuBool's B in batch-37. decisions.json already marks this id as a duplicate of cuBool, so verify.py apply will fold it regardless of this verdict.

tier_reason: First-party README charts only (docs/stats/rq1_rel.png and rq3_int.png): speedup over LAGraph (SuiteSparse) with machine configurations but no compiler or flags, and the harness that ran LAGraph, GraphBLAST and Gunrock is not in the repo. No peer-reviewed spla paper was found, so C. The verdict is downgrade because the PageRank range was overstated and the integrated-GPU chart, where spla loses to LAGraph on most BFS, SSSP and TC runs, was left out.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README log-scale chart (docs/stats/rq1_rel.png) of speedup over LAGraph (SuiteSparse) on a 4-core i7-6700, with spla on a GTX 1070. Values are read off the axis, so approximate. PageRank about 7.5x (coAuthorsCiteseer) to about 50x (coPapersDBLP, com-Orkut) on 12 graphs. SSSP about 1.4x (indochina-2004) to about 23x (road_central). Triangle counting about 4x to 12x. BFS about 0.7x to 3.7x, slower than LAGraph on coAuthorsCiteseer, belgium_osm, com-Orkut and indochina-2004. In PageRank spla beats Gunrock on every graph but trails GraphBLAST on several (e.g. belgium_osm, roadNet-CA, cit-Patents). The second chart (docs/stats/rq3_int.png) runs spla on the integrated GPU of the same machine as LAGraph. There spla is slower than LAGraph on every BFS run (about 0.1x to 0.8x), on most SSSP runs, and on every TC run on the AMD Ryzen 9 7900X/GFX1036 (about 0.1x to 0.3x). It is faster for PageRank (about 2.7x to 11.6x on the i7/HD 530, about 0.8x to 4x on the Ryzen). The README's 'much faster than scipy or networkx' has no numbers behind it.
corrections.caveats: Numbers exist only as chart images (docs/stats/rq1_rel.png, rq3_int.png); all values are read off log or linear axes. The headline comparison is a GTX 1070 GPU against LAGraph on a 4-core CPU, not like for like. In the integrated-GPU comparison, where both run on one device, spla loses to LAGraph on most BFS, SSSP and TC runs and wins only PageRank. The harness for the LAGraph, GraphBLAST and Gunrock runs is not in the repo (only examples/), and compiler, flags, LAGraph/SuiteSparse versions and thread counts are not stated. The README says the project is under heavy development and not ready for usage.

notes: The BFS, SSSP and TC ranges match the chart. The PageRank top end (65x) appears to have been read from the axis limit or GraphBLAST's cit-Patents bar; spla's highest PR bar is about 50x. Shortcoming worth recording: the integrated-GPU chart shows spla slower than LAGraph on most non-PageRank runs. License MIT, 35 stars, 18 forks, last commit 2025-11-17 (active) confirmed.
